newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH DEPUTIES AGAINST CORPORATE TAX CUT IN 1998.
newsitem.headline: POLISH DEPUTIES AGAINST CORPORATE TAX CUT IN 1998.

text.p: Polish parliamentary committees will ask the full house to reject a government proposal of a cut in corporate income tax in 1998 when Sejm, lower house votes next week on tax bills, PAP news agency reported.

PAP said deputies from the budget and finance, economic policy and legislative committees voted to throw out a government proposal to begin lowering the corporate income tax, now at 40 percent, in 1998. The government's long-term economic plan calls for a gradual reduction in corporate taxes to 32 percent in 2001.
The deputies also agreed on a proposal to include in the next year's tax bill a pledge to lower personal income taxes by one point to 20 percent, 32 percent and 44 percent.
The parliament is due to hold the final vote on the 1997 tax package next week.
